dimensions.note: The configured Swamp/agent subprocess intentionally inherits the host environment for provider authentication. Raw subprocess stdout/stderr are no longer persisted, and the README now requires trusted executable configuration and narrowly scoped benchmark credentials, but a compromised configured executable or agent implementation still has the host process credential authority. This cannot be removed here without breaking environment-authenticated providers; integration must use a dedicated least-privilege agent runtime.
Structured info logs cover suite start, every terminal case, and suite completion without prompts, credentials, verifier output, or subprocess output.

Validation/preflight failures occur before writes; per-case failures have deterministic precedence. Cancellation raised during case work no longer becomes infrastructure_error, and cleanup runs in finally.

All 17 tests pass, covering fixtures, strict inputs, path boundaries, status precedence, cancellation, response/actor success, scope violation, timeout, missing artifacts, malformed response, no-change, hidden failure, verifier-output redaction, and workspace cleanup.

A suiteId is a one-run identity: duplicate live paths fail closed rather than overwrite evidence. Generated IDs include timestamp plus UUID entropy; candidate/task IDs are unique and resource identities include suite, candidate, and task. Partial completed cases are durable while temporary workspace state is removed.
The extension makes no direct HTTP API calls; agent interaction is through the typed Swamp CLI model envelope, which is Zod-validated before use.

Deno.Command output capture is byte-bounded while streams are drained, Linux children run in a new process group, cancellation/timeout sends SIGTERM then SIGKILL, timers/listeners are cleared, sandbox tests have 30s bounds, hidden directories are removed per case, and the entire suite workspace is now removed on every exit path.

Fixtures are synthetic and documentation uses placeholder candidate/model identities. The README now states that bundled hardening verifier source is execution-hidden rather than cryptographically secret and that cost/output limits are scoring bounds, not provider spend controls.

All Zod objects are strict-by-default objects with no passthrough. Mechanical schema/write review found 1:1 fields for caseResult and suiteSummary; evidence is a declared JSON file spec. No capped collection silently claims completeness.
caseResult, suiteSummary, and evidence all declare 365d lifetime and bounded garbageCollection counts; non-durable local suite files are now removed in finally.
This is an append-only benchmark execution model, not a remote-resource CRUD lifecycle. It produces immutable run evidence and summaries.

Before candidate execution or data writes, preflight verifies the configured agent model and executes a Bubblewrap/Node smoke test with clear environment, unshared namespaces, read-only binds, and a timeout.

case and evidence identities are evidence/case-suiteId-candidateId-taskId; summary is summary-suiteId. Input schemas reject duplicate candidates/tasks and suite paths reject replay overwrite, so incompatible instances cannot collide.
Methods do not read prior stored state or access dataRepository directly; each suite is an independent append-only execution.
Version 2026.08.19.2 has an explicit upgrade entry; newly added executionMode and tiered score fields have defaults compatible with existing attributes.
